item.title: Untitled feature project #1
item.description:
This is a 120 pages full-movie script telling the story of ...

Legend has it that there is a Samasara Mountain in the middle sea, where people can meet their passed beloved ones. FRAN, an excellent dockyard worker, spends his whole lifetime building Luna May, the strongest flying ship ever, hoping to meet his dad once again. When he is about to depart, DIEGO, a famous traveler and the future-son-in-law to the dockyard’s owner, pressures Fran to sell the ship. Fran flees on Luna May with JULY, a boy he acquaints with back at the dockyard. What he does not know is that July is in fact JUNE - a girl, and what’s more, Diego’s fiancée.

item.description:
This is a 30 pages short-film script telling the story of ...

Do you remember the feeling of the last several semi-conscious minutes before fully waking up, when the dream and reality are mixed together? NARCIS is a superstar. D-Day of his most important tour, his world starts to disappear; everything and every relationship of his plunges into chaos - his autographing session, his manager, his band, his girlfriend… Narcis believes it’s only a terrible dream, so he tries to wake himself up; but the more he struggles, the worse the situtation will become.

item.title: Fluid Simulation
item.description: Inspired by the marbling art, we aimed at generate real-time multi-fluid effects interacted with web-cam captured motion. We combine the real-time optical flow estimation into the advection process of fast 2D fluid simulation and achieve fancy fluid simulation. Dec. 2016

item.title: Semantic Focal Stack Analysis
item.description: Stereo matching typically involves assigning each pixel a discrete disparity label from a finite set. We present a novel approach that uses scene semantic labeling for finding an appropriate disparity label set that accelerates matching and improves accuracy. Using a light field as input, our semantic focal stack analysis (SFSA) first locates salient objects and then estimate their approximate disparities. Disparity redistribution is then conducted to more densely sample disparity labels at the detected salient objects.
